## Issue 235 attempt 2: fit from the true perturbed start (2 November 2026)

**Outcome: different endpoint; the fitting path is not qualified by this
attempt.** The fit started where it was declared to start and returned the same
cost as attempt 1 within the 1e-6 band, with the same six active bounds. All eight
free (interior) coordinates did not recover attempt 1 within **1e-5 scaled units**: the
largest difference is **0.0499 scales** (bicarbonate–water `k_ij`), about 5000
times the tolerance. Under the accepted plan, a coordinate mismatch is a
different endpoint even when the cost agrees.

The start was correct this time. Engine inferred an optimizer start of exactly
**0** in all 14 entries from the physical start document
([`inputs/fit-start.json`](inputs/fit-start.json), $q^*+s\,d$ for each named
target, including the 0.88 and 1 diameter ties) and the Engine-completed
starting laws in [`declarations-fit.toml`](declarations-fit.toml). The native
`FitResult.initial_cost` was **45.89741010758851**, against
**45.897410107590936** from fresh predictions of the start document and laws:
a relative difference of **5.27e-14**, limit 1e-8. The starting physical values,
ties and R2/R5 coefficients matched their declarations with zero error. All 213
start rows were available, the 213 × 14 derivatives were finite, and the start
weighted residuals differed from the baseline by norm **0.98276** (limit 1e-4).
The fit declaration differs from the endpoint declaration in only two ways: the
starting R2/R5 laws, and an explicit `inputs/endpoint.json` construction
document for the 200 datasets that previously inherited the selected parameter
document. Observation construction is therefore unchanged when the start is
selected. The baseline again reproduced #233 at **45.37796168239802**
(1.66e-13 relative).

Group costs after attempt 2, with changes from the start and from attempt 1:
common149 23.832044071 (−0.332799; −3.20e-4), restored species 2.447297350
(+0.066829; −2.72e-5), Jakobsen 13.138819875 (−0.251321; +3.34e-4), loaded
density 0.565279802 (−0.012906; −3.06e-5), and Cp 5.377084829 (−0.006687;
+4.40e-5). The two endpoints redistribute fit quality among the groups by
amounts of order 1e-4 while their total cost differs by only 3.08e-7.

**Interpretation.** The coordinate difference aligns with locally weak
directions of the 213-row objective at the attempt 2 endpoint, consistent with
function-tolerance termination. This local evidence does not establish the
objective's shape between the endpoints, a common basin, or the absence of a
fitting-path defect.
A post-run reduction of the retained Jacobian at the attempt 2 endpoint
([`weak-direction.json`](results/fit-true-start-e6dae5c7/weak-direction.json);
array reduction only, no Engine call) puts **70 %** of the squared coordinate
difference on the weakest singular direction ($\sigma=8.99\times10^{-4}$) and
**93 %** on the weakest two. That weakest direction is dominated by
bicarbonate–water `k_ij` (component −0.82), with the two enthalpy shifts
(−0.35 each). The quadratic residual-sensitivity term
$\tfrac12\lVert J\,\Delta z\rVert^2=1.76\times10^{-7}$ is a diagnostic only, not
an estimate of the cost change: the linear term $r^\mathsf{T}J\,\Delta z$
($-8.72\times10^{-7}$ at endpoint 2 toward endpoint 1, independent review) is
larger in magnitude. The full-chart singular vectors include active-bound
coordinates, so they are not unconstrained parameter uncertainties. Both runs stopped on function tolerance
with projected-gradient norms near 1e-4, so neither stopping point is shown to
be an exact minimizer. The 1e-5 coordinate tolerance along this
direction was not met by function-tolerance termination here. The design
anticipated this outcome, and the result is retained without relaxing the
tolerance. The two endpoints differ by 5.0e-4 in bicarbonate–water `k_ij` at a cost
difference of 3.1e-7; how strongly the retained rows determine that parameter
is not established by this local evidence.
This is local numerical sensitivity, not an estimated parameter uncertainty.

Evidence type: numerical verification of start selection, replay and endpoint
reproducibility for one local fit. It is not physical validation, parameter
adoption, an identifiability proof or a fitted-document export. No numerical
uncertainty estimate was made. No further attempt follows automatically; any
change of tolerance, stopping rule or comparison basis is an owner/Design
decision.

## Issue 235 bounded fit on Engine e6dae5c7 (2 November 2026)

**Outcome: invalid coordinate/law declaration; the fitting path is not
qualified by this attempt.** Native fitting did not begin at the declared
perturbed origin. Its starting cost was **45.377961682398116**, the accepted
endpoint chart cost (design probe: 45.37796168239813), whereas the
independently evaluated perturbed start is **45.897410107590936**. The relative
difference is **0.01132**, against the 1e-8 limit. Engine computes the starting
optimizer as $(q_{\mathrm{start}}-o_i)/s_i$ from the start parameter document
and the problem reaction laws (`engine/native/regression/coordinates.cpp`,
lines 133–152, at e6dae5c7). Binding the start to the accepted document while
encoding perturbed origins therefore starts at $v=-d$, the accepted endpoint,
not at optimizer zero. The design assumed the declared origin would be the
fitting start; this attempt shows otherwise. The cause is identified; changing
the start declaration is a Design decision, and any further fitting attempt
requires owner authorization.

The chart itself was verified at optimizer zero: all 18 physical rows equal the
perturbation table and its 0.88/1 ties exactly, the completed R2/R5 laws equal
the design probe, all 213 rows and 213 × 14 residual derivatives are finite, and
the weighted residuals differ from the baseline by norm **0.98276** (limit 1e-4).
The baseline reproduced #233 at cost **45.37796168239802**
(1.66e-13 relative); maximum relative prediction change 6.96e-13 and maximum
scaled residual/row-cost changes 7.06e-12 and 5.44e-12, inside the 1e-10 rule.

Starting effectively from the accepted endpoint, the single fit returned these
values on the same 213-row objective with 14 coordinates:

| Quantity | Value | Limit |
|---|---:|---|
| Native termination | converged, usable; function tolerance 1.62e-9 ≤ 1e-8 | usable converged |
| Iterations; residual/Jacobian evaluations; trial failures | 6; 7/6; 0 | ≤ 60 |
| Final dimensionless cost | 45.360525618233154 | ≤ 45.37800706035217 |
| Change from accepted endpoint | −0.017436064 (−0.0384 %) | — |
| Replay cost difference, relative | 7.74e-14 | ≤ 1e-8 |
| Maximum replay weighted-residual difference | 5.84e-12 | ≤ 1e-8 absolute |
| Maximum $\lvert(q_f-q^*)/s\rvert$ | 3.454 (R2 enthalpy shift) | ≤ 1 |
| Rank; condition number; smallest singular value | 14; 18552.2; 8.98e-4 | reported |
| Projected-gradient norm | 1.398e-4 | reported |

Group costs after the fit, with change from the baseline: common149
23.832364343 (−0.028632), restored species 2.447324544 (−0.001350), Jakobsen
13.138485509 (+0.016303), loaded density 0.565310401 (−0.000093), and Cp
5.377040821 (−0.003664). Six coordinates end on bounds: MEAH+–water and
carbamate–MEAH+ `k_ij`, the MEAH+ segment diameter, both Born diameters, and
the R2 incremental enthalpy shift at **−8636.07 J/mol** (total −10000 J/mol,
its declared lower bound). The R5 incremental shift moved to
**−8360.36 J/mol** (3.34 scales) and bicarbonate–water `k_ij` from 0.72706 to
0.70410 (2.30 scales). The lower cost is therefore obtained outside the
one-scale neighborhood, mostly through the reaction-enthalpy coordinates; the
cost decrease is small compared with those displacements, consistent with the
weakly determined directions in the singular values.

This is numerical evidence about one local fit of the reduced objective, not
physical validation, parameter adoption or a new parameter set. It does not
answer the issue's question, which concerns a fit from the perturbed start; the
lower-cost endpoint is retained as observed behavior, not as a qualified result.
Completed laws returned by Engine carry one observation's 293.15–393.15 K
domain; the corrected `fitted_reactions` kept each destination's bounds
(393.15 and 436.85 K) during replay. No numerical uncertainty estimate was made.
A table is used because the result is a few scalar comparisons; a plot would
not clarify where the fit started.

## Issue 235 design replay on Engine e6dae5c7 (2 November 2026)

**The owner accepted the 213-row e6dae5c7 baseline on 2 November 2026.**
At the unchanged endpoint its dimensionless cost is **45.37796168239802**,
against **45.37796168239049**, an absolute increase of
$7.531752999057062\times10^{-12}$ and relative change of
$1.659\times10^{-13}$. Every row is available and meets its native
requested tolerance. Two rows exceeded the original $10^{-10}$ relative comparison for residuals
and row costs. That original comparison is retained below for traceability;
the owner replaced it with the rule stated beside this evidence.

| Field | Largest relative change | Target |
|---|---:|---|
| Prediction | 6.95644483271666e-13 | `vle_obs_0133-pco2` |
| Residual | 1.2627348373152909e-10 | `vle_obs_0124-pco2` |
| Weighted residual | 1.2627357231932254e-10 | `vle_obs_0124-pco2` |
| Row cost | 2.525470820199663e-10 | `vle_obs_0124-pco2` |

For the largest row-cost change, the new value is
**1.1982922885866476e-5**, versus **1.1982922882840224e-5** retained,
an absolute difference of **3.026252208895852e-15**.
`vinjarapu2024_source_table4_06` also exceeded the original row-cost comparison
(**1.6304899911582942e-10** relative). This is numerical verification
at a fixed endpoint; the small absolute differences do not identify their
cause or establish physical validation. No numerical uncertainty estimate
was made.

[Baseline differences, group costs and input hashes](results/design-replay-e6dae5c7/baseline.json)
and [all 213 predictions](results/design-replay-e6dae5c7/predictions.json)
retain this single rerun. Python 3.13.14, NumPy 2.5.4 and SciPy 1.18.1
were used in an isolated environment with Engine **1.2.0**, merged commit
`e6dae5c7353ae10e0aa2d8e46055847b9d64bbe4`, wheel SHA-256
`83ede7d2722d3581603f6e4139c614b8bbfc903ce90609c90b802d46eea77dd6`.
Installed Engine files were byte-compared with the supplied wheel.
The scratch command ran through `agent-heavy`; active wall time was
**4.989714511 s** including packet construction, excluding environment setup
and memory admission. No input, root dependency pin or Engine source changed.

The owner-approved replay rule from 2 November 2026 is **1e-10 relative on
predicted values and total cost**. Residuals, weighted residuals and row costs
are compared using $|\Delta|\le10^{-10}\max(|\mathrm{reference}|,1)$.
For a log-ratio residual, its relative change divides the relative prediction
change by $|r|$. Near-zero residuals therefore amplify that comparison;
`vle_obs_0124-pco2` has a residual of approximately −0.00147. This explains the
sensitivity of the comparison, **not the cause of the approximately 1e-13
prediction change, which was not diagnosed**. The accepted baseline cost and
prediction differences satisfy the revised rule. The raw evidence is unchanged.

The earlier stop at baseline replay is superseded by this owner decision.
The continuation checks below concern coordinate evaluation and the prescribed
start only. Build ceilings remain **170 executable lines plus 20 test lines;
30 min total, 20 min native fitting, 60 iterations**. No fitting ran.
Independent readiness review and publication of the accepted issue body remain
with the accountable owner. No manuscript promotion is claimed.
The existing 307-row historical result below retains its original wheel identity;
the 94 neutral rows were not rerun here. No site refresh or manuscript index
change was made in this design-only task.

## Coordinate-aware start check for issue 235

**The merged e6dae5c7 wheel accepts all 213 unchanged reactive observations
with the 14 declared coordinates at both the accepted endpoint and the
prescribed perturbed start.** This is numerical verification of evaluation and
local derivatives; no optimization or physical validation was performed.
The original R2/R5 declarations remain unchanged: each has 200 rows with
293.15–393.15 K bounds and 13 rows with 293.15–436.85 K bounds. Those broader
construction bounds do not establish physical validity above 393.15 K.

| Quantity | Accepted-endpoint chart | Prescribed-start chart |

| Weighted-residual norm | 9.52659033257945 | 9.580961340866427 |
| Weighted Jacobian rank | 14 of 14 | 14 of 14 |
| Smallest singular value | 0.0008323585689863121 | 0.0008252288917842002 |

| Coordinate evaluation and differentiation, active seconds | 7.929813417 | 7.886433574 |

The weighted-residual difference norm is **0.9827591589164358**, exceeding the
required **1e-4**. All 213 × 14 returned residual-derivative entries are finite
at each point. The endpoint chart predictions differ from the original #233
reference by at most **7.262194859872024e-13 relative**; total cost differs by
**1.6830981053317373e-13 relative**. Maximum differences divided by
$\max(|\mathrm{reference}|,1)$ are **7.062572748850471e-12** for residuals
and weighted residuals and **5.444256157005611e-12** for row costs. These satisfy
the owner-approved replay rule. The differentiation baseline and earlier
fixed replay are separate evaluations; neither replaces the other's records.

The probe used `reg.differentiate` with observations, optimizer zero, no holds
and the fixed thermal record. `reg.evaluate_coordinates` alone returned an
empty `reaction_laws` mapping at both points. Observation-aware differentiation
returned completed R2 and R5 laws. Their standard-state identities agree with
both original destination sets:
`aqueous-molality-infinite-dilution-water-v1`. Reference temperature remains
313.15 K. At the prescribed −250 J/mol incremental shift for each reaction,
R2 has `a=23.48949797584855`, `b=-11897.988648703167 K`; R5 has
`a=2.8538383112075874`, `b=-7674.6101162509585 K`, including its simultaneous
coefficient perturbation. Full coefficients and physical coordinate values
are retained; no local reaction-law composition was substituted for Engine.

The [revised design](FIT-CHECK-DESIGN.md) preserves the perturbation table as

copy only coefficients and their reference-temperature representation, preserve
each destination's bounds, and reject a standard-state mismatch. One two-domain

No executable repository code or persistent test was changed. The design
keeps the 170 executable-line ceiling and all approved time/iteration limits.
No budget increase is proposed. Independent readiness review, accepted issue
publication and the bounded fitting attempt remain outstanding. No parameter

## Result and intended use

The generic solvent-specification driver reproduces **all 307 objective rows
exactly**, at dimensionless cost **148.87893934557388**.
The largest relative difference is zero for every prediction, residual,
weighted residual and row cost. All rows are `Available` and meet their native
requested numerical tolerance. There is no first differing target.

This is numerical verification of declaration mapping at the supplied endpoint,
not independent physical validation. No fit, parameter adoption, manuscript
change, phase search or absorber qualification was performed. The published
[issue #236](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/236)
owns the scope and comparison tolerance, $10^{-10}$ relative per field.

[Continuation results](results/continuation.json) retain all 39 native solves
and incoming pressure, supported mole fractions and packing fractions. Four
isotherms start independently, without a predecessor. Maximum absolute native
residual is $5.684341886080802\times10^{-14}$. Preparation compared both original
source guesses and runtime continuation declarations against their owners.

All 25 Cai pairs have identical problem declarations and construction parameters.
The paired native temperature predictions range from 363.18157890248386 to

Their [prediction records](results/predictions.json) retain the temperature

[Failure checks](results/failure-checks.json) retain a fixed-temperature refusal,

Every later member of that isotherm becomes dependent unavailable with the
